about: lib/product-pricing.js priceProduct and labour ONCE per product (Turki, Nov 19; data model: Mac Figma p.18). A product with its own `rates` costs each part's material, wear and power by its own print time, and the labour, (prep + post) × rate × (1 + failure/100), once. `labourPerPart: true` puts labour back in every part. A product with NO `rates` (every product saved before this) costs exactly as before. One part here: 100 g of 90/1000 g filament (9.00), 2 h at wear 0.75 (1.50) and 150 W × 0.18 (0.054), +10% failure = 11.6094 without labour; labour 0.75 h × 90 × 1.1 = 74.25. The Mac and the phone run this file. Money review of #2575: the shop packaging is charged ONCE with the labour (per part only under labourPerPart); a part's own prep/post is not used under once-labour; productJobParts gives a job the parts costed without labour and packaging and the labour and packaging as ORDER-level costs (labourCost, packagingCost: never a part, Dev Hub Nov 19), so newOrder prices it exactly as the catalogue.

cases.why: a single item: the catalogue costs it exactly as the calculator does (11.61 + 74.25)
labourPerPart: the explicit override puts labour back in every part: 15 × 85.86
LEGACY: a product with no rates (6 parts carrying their own) costs exactly as before: 6 × 85.86, no silent re-price
a part's own rate wins over the product's: one part at 120 W instead of 150 changes only its power
PACKAGING once: 15 parts with packaging 5 cost 15 × 11.61 + 74.25 + 5 × 1.1 (was 15 × 5.50 of packaging)
a PART's own prep time is not used under once-labour: part 4 with prep 2 h still costs 248.39

JOB == CATALOGUE: a job taken from a 15-part product through productJobParts (15 parts, labour 74.25 and packaging 5.50 at the ORDER level) is priced by newOrder at the catalogue's base price (330.06)
